key_insight: Molecularly confined water at 2D material interfaces exhibits nonlinear, soft-glassy rheology and a pressure-induced slowdown with relaxation times reaching microseconds.
engineering_relevance: Pressure- and material-dependent water dynamics could enable tunable nonlinear nanofluidic elements.
method: Use tuning-fork-based atomic force microscopy to probe confined water.
Measure shear-dependent viscoelasticity from linear to nonlinear response across different 2D interfaces.
Model the response using shear-induced acceleration of relaxation dynamics.
evidence_signal: Measurements reveal pronounced rate effects, microsecond relaxation times, and material-dependent dynamics, with the observed rheology captured by a nonlinear model.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative pressure ranges or device-scale validation, limiting assessment of practical operating conditions.
paper_title: Dramatic pressure-induced slowdown and the soft glassy rheology of water at 2D material interface
